**What it is:** a local Python command-line tool (standard library only, no network). It reads your missed-question journal (`seed/missed.json`) and prints a 3 to 30 day NCLEX-PN study plan. The plan:
- sorts each miss by why it slipped: knowledge gap, misread question, scope confusion or test anxiety;
- mixes client-need categories across the study days instead of doing one category at a time;
- brings each topic back for review 1 and 3 days later;
- names a "focus of the day" that rotates through your 3 weakest client needs;
- ends with a Tighten up day and a Check-in day;
- lists topics you've missed more than once, even when spelled differently;
- has options to filter by topic or date (`--topic`, `--since`) and a screen-reader layout (`--plain`).

**Rules we're under**
- **No paid qbank content**, not even paraphrased. Tags and your own notes only. The loader rejects entries that look like question stems, answer options or rationales.
- **PN scope wording only** (reinforce, monitor, report, follow the care plan). Code checks and tests enforce it.
- **Plain JSON you can edit on a phone.** No database.
- **No gamification.** The only exception is the "days studied in a row" counter. The leaderboard stays parked.
- **Local only.** No packaging, no GitHub.
- **Nurse review before anyone else sees it.**

I added `--weeks W` as a shorthand for `--days` W × 7, and all 177 tests pass. I also confirmed that `--weeks 4` produces exactly the same plan as `--days 28`.

**How it works**
- **Allowed values:** 1 to 4 weeks. `--days` only goes up to 30, so 5 weeks (35 days) doesn't fit.
- **Mistakes get the same kind of explanation `--days` gives:**
  - `--weeks 5` or `--weeks 0`: "use a whole number of weeks from 1 to 4 (7 to 28 days); got 5. Plans run 3 to 30 days; use --days for a length that isn't whole weeks."
  - `--weeks 1.5` or `two`: it shows what you typed.
- **Using both is refused:** `--weeks 2 --days 10` gives "argument --days: not allowed with argument --weeks".

**Everything else is the same:** I ran the 13 saved command-line scenarios before and after the change. The only difference is the usage and help text, which now show `[--days N | --weeks W]`. Plan wording didn't change, so the review code is still `a63b6b654811`.

**Tests:** six new tests check that:
- 1 to 4 weeks give the same plan as the matching `--days`, including with `--plain`, `--start` and `--topic`;
- out-of-range values and values that aren't whole numbers get the explanations above;
- `--weeks` and `--days` can't be used together;
- the 1 to 4 range stays inside the `--days` range.

One extra test I wrote was wrong: it assumed the word "week" never appears in plan wording, but "next week" already does. I deleted it; the unchanged review code covers the same point.

**Docs:** I added a note to the README, a CHANGELOG entry for 0.3.2, and bumped the version to 0.3.2.

**Still open, unchanged:**

A local Python CLI for your NCLEX-PN study. It reads `missed.json`, your journal of missed practice questions (tags and your own notes only), and builds a study plan of 3 to 30 days. It uses only the Python standard library and never touches the network.

## Rules

The journal holds only tags and your own notes, never question text, answer options or rationales from UWorld, Archer, Kaplan or any other paid qbank, not even paraphrased. `journal.py` refuses entries that look like qbank text. 3. **Plain JSON storage** that you can edit on your phone. No database, no binary formats.
4. **No gamification.** The one exception is the "days studied in a row" counter.
